evidence: M-O s.v. political division: county; county (domain of count)
terms.comment: From comes, a count: the land a count governed, and so an English shire (Lüders 1826, of Dorset and Gloucestershire) and a subdivision of a US state (M-O). Classically comitātus is an escort, a retinue (Lewis & Short), so make the sense clear the first time.

evidence: Caes. BG 1.12.4: in quattuor pāgōs dīvīsa est
terms.comment: Caesar’s word for the districts into which a Gallic people was divided, the nearest classical thing to a county; also the country as against the town, and the villagers themselves (Lewis & Short). A county council: see council.

phrases.latin: nam omnis cīvitās Helvētia in quattuor pāgōs dīvīsa est
phrases.english: for the whole Helvetian state is divided into four districts
